title: Natural Selection: The Engine of Evolution Practice Exam
description: Recall and guided drill for Natural Selection: The Engine of Evolution.

questions.question: Which condition is required for natural selection?
options: traits changing because organisms want them

questions.question: Populations evolve over generations; individual organisms do not evolve during their lifetime.
questions.explanation: Evolution refers to population change across generations.

questions.question: A trait that improves reproductive success in a specific environment can increase an organism's ________.
questions.explanation: Fitness means reproductive success in context.

questions.question: Which example best shows selection pressure?
questions.explanation: The antibiotic affects survival of bacteria with different traits.

questions.question: Explain why existing variation matters in natural selection.
questions.correctAnswer: Variation matters because the environment can only favor traits already present in the population.
questions.explanation: Natural selection acts on existing heritable differences.

questions.question: In natural selection, what usually becomes more common over generations?
options: heritable traits that improve survival or reproduction
traits learned only by one individual
features unrelated to reproduction in every environment
questions.explanation: Helpful heritable traits tend to increase.

questions.question: Natural selection plans ahead for what a species will need in the future.
questions.explanation: Natural selection has no plan; it filters existing variation.

questions.question: Use antibiotic resistance to summarize natural selection in one sentence.
questions.correctAnswer: Resistant bacteria survive antibiotic treatment better and reproduce, so resistance becomes more common over generations.
questions.explanation: The sentence should include survival, reproduction, and population change.
